newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges move lower with crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges move lower with crude.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges moved lower in early trade on Friday on the back of weaker demand after crude's fall overnight, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $84 and $83.50 a tonne fob ARA a few times, or some $1.50 to $2 below Thursday's closing level. Later talk was said to be $84/$84.50.
"Demand is weak; technically numb," one trader said.
"The market is dead. It has been quiet all week," a second trader said.

"Someone bought yesterday at $85 and $85.50 to push up the market but then crude fell hard last night, so that is why it (high sulphur) weakened. There is no demand today, no enquiries, maybe only 8,000 tonnes."

Low sulphur fuel oil barges were offered a little weaker after crude weakened, with sellers slashing 50 cents to $1 off their asking prices, to $96.50 and $96 but not too much buying interest was seen at those levels.
"There were no deals so far today...I think people may be waiting for prices to drop further with crude," one Rotterdam-based trader said.
High sulphur cargoes were said to be unchanged with the good supply of Russian being absorbed by the market but some pressure was said to be looming if prompt cargoes went unsold.

One seller was heard to be holding three prompt cargoes of M-100 Russian, two cracked and one straight-run, loading in early July. The seller had moved from $81.50/$82 cif to a floating price earlier this week.
